# Your lame foot

### *[October of Zarathustra](https://bradydale.com/series-october-of-zarathustra.html)*

No obituary has ever haunted me more than [that of Bill Smith](https://www.economist.com/obituary/2011/10/22/bill-smith), from a 2011 issue of *The Economist* ([archive link](https://archive.ph/8UogW)). Smith was an amateur Fell runner.

The fells are rocky, mountainous lands in England and Scotland. Rainy. Damp. Full of danger.

Smith devoted his life to running across them through the weekends, often alone. Jumping across crevices or climbing when two feet weren't enough. To run the fells one used studded shoes. He ran races and he ran in clubs, but what the obituary brings out is that he just did it for the love of the game.

He wrote a 600-page book about running out there and gave all the proceeds to the running association. During the week, he had a laborer's job at a department store. He had no aspirations to anything more. All he wanted was to stay fit and enjoy the lands he loved the most.

And he died out there. Somewhere on the fells, on his way to watch a race, something went wrong and that's where he fell, aged 75. The lands he loved kept him forever.

Smith literally went over and went under, again and again, up the hills, down into the bogs. He took himself lightly in this account. He loved his hobby. It gave his life meaning. It wasn't about him, it's just what he wanted to do.

To my read, there are three parts to Zarathustra's speech to the higher men in his cave at the end of the book.

* First, the mob will never understand you.
* Second, to strive means to likely fail.
* Third, but it doesn't matter if you fail, so laugh, or dance.

Or run.

"Dig deep, lad."

## One line

> “Freedom from fever is far from being knowledge! I do not believe frozen spirits. He who cannot lie does not know what truth is.” —Zarathustra

—Brady Dale  
October 27, 2026
